title: The Fior
summary: Trial by ordeal among the fae.

claims.text: Noble courts judge fairly but finally; since King David's reforms the accused may have counsel and may choose summary judgment or trial by Fior.

The Fior is an old noble custom of trial by ordeal, also used by many commoner courts and motleys, and not only in law: a suitor may be set a Fior by the one being courted. A graver crime demands a harder test, often one that makes the accused face the wrong done.

title: Noble political leanings
summary: Reformers, Modernists and the Beltaine Blade.

claims.text: The Beltaine Blade gathers the most reactionary nobles.
Reformers want a constitutional monarchy, led by philosopher-kings and answerable to what the people want; King David and Queen Mab are leading examples, though Reformers differ a great deal.
Modernists, rare among sidhe, accept or even embrace the modern world, a risky course given sidhe frailty before Banality; House Scathach leans Modernist.
